figures.alt: Five kinds of clues flow into the phone and become one best guess: the blue dot

figures.caption: **Figure 1. Where each clue works.** Satellites outdoors, Wi-Fi in town, beacons in some stores, cell towers almost everywhere, and motion sensors in between. Not to scale.
figures.alt: Walking from a field into town and into a store, a different clue is strongest in each place

figures.caption: **Figure 2. Why indoors is different.** Satellite signals are faint by the time they reach a roof. The Wi-Fi is inside with you. Not to scale.
figures.alt: Indoors, satellite signals are faint after the roof. The Wi-Fi access point is inside with you. The cell tower is far off.

figures.caption: **Figure 3. Building the map, using the map.** The phone never joins these networks. It only hears them. Two-step idea after David Coleman. Not to scale.
figures.alt: Step 1: phones that know where they are note the Wi-Fi they hear and send it to the map. Step 2: a phone indoors hears the same Wi-Fi, looks it up, and finds its spot

figures.caption: **Figure 4. Through the lobby door.** Your phone leans on satellites outside and Wi-Fi inside, so the dot holds steady. Not to scale.
figures.alt: Walking in through a lobby door, the phone swaps satellites for Wi-Fi and the dot holds steady

figures.caption: **Figure 5. The circle around the dot.** The circle shows how sure your phone is. A small circle means it's confident. A big circle means it's guessing. Not to scale.
figures.alt: A small circle means the phone is sure. A big circle means it is guessing. Step toward a window or wait, and the circle shrinks

figures.caption: **Figure 6. Precise location, on and off.** With it off, an app still knows your area, but not your door. Not to scale.
figures.alt: With precise location on, an app sees your door. With it off, the app sees only your area

figures.caption: **Figure 7. The Wi-Fi button in Control Center doesn't turn Wi-Fi off.** To turn Wi-Fi all the way off, go to {{Settings}} > {{Wi-Fi}}.
figures.alt: The Control Center Wi-Fi button only disconnects; the phone still hears Wi-Fi and uses it for location. Turning Wi-Fi off in Settings stops that

figures.caption: **Figure 8. One change to the name.** The password stays the same. Only the end of the name changes.
figures.alt: Add _nomap to the end of your Wi-Fi name and Apple and Google leave it off their maps

figures.caption: **Figure 9. A 911 call, in the US.** Your phone works out where it is, sends that spot with the call, and the call goes to the 911 center near you.
figures.alt: On a 911 call, the phone works out where it is and sends that spot with the call to the 911 center near you, even with location turned off

figures.caption: **Figure 10. Which way to call.** The phone's own dialer sends your spot with the call.
figures.alt: Call 911 from the phone's own dialer: it sends your spot. A messaging app may not

figures.caption: **Figure 11. Anyone walking by.** A passing phone can add your router to the map. Not to scale.
figures.alt: Any phone walking past your house can add your Wi-Fi to the map
